How about just getting rid of "shadow banning" on voat? If someone is banned, even if the reason is obvious they should be notified and told why.

@Atko:

Shadowbanning is effective against spammers (actual spammers which submit, say, viagra ads).

Why can't we let spammers know that their spam account is banned?

Because letting spammers know that their account is banned - will not have them think "oh, my viagra ad campaign was banned. I should stop submitting". Instead, they will think "oh, my viagra ad was banned, it is time to make a new account so that I can spam my viagra ads again".

Key issues:

  • moderators have the ability to ban people from subs they moderate.
  • banned people are not notified that they are banned for reasons described above
  • moderators can abuse their power

Possible solutions? Let the community decide what is spam so that they can downvote spam? This may work some day, but not while voat is a small community, mostly because many people can't even downvote (low CCP).

Downvoting spam does not remove spam from showing up in /v/all/new. Should we hide submissions from /v/all/new if they get X downvote ratio? Isn't this censorship too and wouldn't this be abused by organized groups?

My proposed solution:

* moderator watch mechanism

If a moderator issues a shadowban on a user which has good account reputation (high CCP, good submission record), this moderator should be removed from the sub. This entails responsiblity (who gets to remove moderators and who gets to watch the watchers?) and costs. As voat grows, community management will be a major, ongoing process which requires human resources. Who will pay these people?
